newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Monday mainly because the plunging domestic A share markets failed to support the repo rates despite their low levels, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 7.0 percent from 9.0 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 4.1 million lots from 1.6 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Both Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets plunged on Monday with sentiment hurt by successive losses in the past few days.
"Institutions including securities houses stayed on the sidelines on the repo market on Monday with fund demand decreasing due to the A share market slump," a trader said.

But an issue of 120 million A shares by an A share company on the Shenzhen stock exchange supported some early-maturing contracts in particular the three-day contract, which rose to 7.0 percent from 2.0 percent, traders said.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to move narrowly around the current level in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Monday.
Traders said the slump on the A share markets pushed more liquidity into the spot market, further pushing up prices after successive gains in the past few trading days.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 109.99 yuan from 109.42 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose sharply to 1.09 million lots from 617,837 lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to continue to rise on the back of the bearish stock markets.
